answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat each identity as a vertex in a trust graph, where edges form only through costly verifiable work: completed jobs, staked collateral, or vouches from established peers. A newcomer starts like a sparrow at the flock's edge, free to watch and take tiny tasks, but gains weight only as real counterparties vouch for it. After sustained honest work it earns a violet trust mark, while forging thousands of fake vertices with no genuine history costs more than any of them could ever earn.
